notes: Rochester City Council unanimously approved (Monday, 2026-07-06, per Post Bulletin datePublished) a five-year contract with Via Transit Twin Cities LLC, replacing TransDev/First Transit (whose contract expires 2026-12-31), effective 2026-09-01. Quote: "The council unanimously approved a five-year contract Monday with Via Transit Twin Cities LLC, replacing the current operator, TransDev, on Sept. 1. The contract will provide drivers and other staff for daily operations of the city's fixed-route, paratransit and future bus rapid transit services, as well as maintenance for the city-owned buses." Quote on value/term: "The five-year contract, which is valued at roughly $77.8 million for the expanded services throughout the period, includes the potential for a five-year extension at the end of 2031" -- term_years_incl_options=10 (5 base + 5 option); kttc.com separately describes a "64-month initial term." Buses are city-owned (vehicles_supplied_by=agency); Via supplies drivers/staff/maintenance -> Hybrid, not Turnkey. Covers ZIPS (Zumbro Independent Passenger Service), RPT's ADA paratransit brand referenced in targets.csv, since paratransit is explicitly named in scope -- program_name left blank because the contract is system-wide (fixed-route + paratransit + future Link BRT), not ZIPS-specific. No pricing basis (per-hour vs subscription), funding source, or fleet size stated in either source. Five companies submitted proposals; Mayo Clinic had a representative on the selection panel. DISTINCT from the unrelated 2022/2024 via_news items about Rochester, NY's "RTS On Demand" switching to the Via software platform (T218) -- that is a different Rochester in a different state and a different (software-only) product; not used for this row per the brief's trap warning.

notes: Downtowner, pre-acquisition (award predates Via's 2025-12-12 acquisition of Downtowner, though service launched and the via_news press release covering it are both post-acquisition). Salisbury Post (2025-08-08, describing 'on Tuesday' = 2025-08-05 council meeting): 'The Salisbury City Council approved an approximately $2.8 million contract with Downtowner Holdings on Tuesday...The contract is in the amount of $2,895,000, which is being entirely funded through state and federal grants...The federal funds are $1,158,000. The state funds are $1,737,000 and local funds, our cost in this is zero...the members of the City Council voted unanimously to approve the contract with Downtowner for an amount not to exceed $2,895,000.' Downtowner selected from 3 RFP responses (RFP 029-2024 per salisburync.gov agenda-item link found by search); first NC microtransit program for Downtowner. Service (branded Salisbury Connect) launched 2026-01-19 replacing fixed Route 3 (Blue Route, serving Spencer/East Spencer/VA Medical Center/Novant Health Rowan Medical Center) plus ADA Paratransit. Via press release (ridewithvia.com, 2026-01-15): 'Downtowner Holdings is the microtransit service provider and they will administer operators, vehicles, software, and management for Route 3...and ADA Paratransit service' -- explicit Turnkey marker (operators=drivers, vehicles, software, management all Downtowner). Fleet: 'five Toyota Sienna minivans, which are ADA-compliant.' Promotional fares $1.00 (first 60 days)/$0.50 reduced; no pricing basis (per-hour vs subscription) stated to the agency. No contract term length found. A 2026-05-05 council meeting (per Salisbury Post preview, 2026-05-01) received a financial/statistical update from Downtowner at the ~4-month mark but no new dollar figures were reported in that preview article.
